title: 10,000 flips: do heads and tails meet?
hook: Flip long enough and heads and tails even out. So the gap between them shrinks. Right?

knows: a fair coin lands heads half the time
doesNotKnow: that the law of large numbers concerns proportions, not counts

misconception: The law of large numbers means the heads and tails counts get closer together as you keep flipping.
objective: The learner can explain that the heads share converges to 50% while the heads-minus-tails gap typically grows (like the square root of the number of flips), because the total grows faster than the gap.

claims.text: After n fair flips, the heads-minus-tails gap has a standard deviation of the square root of n: 100 for 10,000 flips.
claims.source: H - T is a sum of n independent +1/-1 steps, each with variance 1, so var = n and SD = sqrt(n); sqrt(10,000) = 100.

claims.text: The average size of the gap is about 2.5 after 10 flips, 8 after 100, 25 after 1,000 and 80 after 10,000.
claims.source: E|H - T| is approximately sqrt(2n/pi): 2.52, 7.98, 25.2, 79.8. Exact binomial sums: n = 10 gives 2.46; n = 10,000 gives 79.79 (computed in node).

claims.text: The heads share after 10,000 fair flips is within about 1 percentage point of 50% in 95% of runs.
claims.source: SD of the share = 0.5/sqrt(10,000) = 0.005; 1.96 x 0.005 = 0.0098, about 1 point.

claims.text: The 20 runs on the stage are seeded fair flips; after 10,000 flips their gaps averaged 86 (largest 204) and every heads share was between 49.0% and 50.9%.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/coin-gap-keeps-growing/model.ts, seed 1713. Re-run: mean |gap| 2.5 / 8.3 / 16.3 / 86.1 at 10 / 100 / 1,000 / 10,000 flips; share range at 10,000: 0.4898-0.5089.

claims.text: The law of large numbers says the share of heads settles toward 50%; it says nothing that requires the counts to come together.
claims.source: W. Feller, An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications, Vol. 1, 3rd ed. (1968), ch. III (fluctuations in coin tossing) and ch. X (law of large numbers).

recall.question: After a million fair coin flips, which is most likely?
options: Heads and tails within a few of each other, and the share very near 50%
Heads and tails hundreds apart, but the share very near 50%
recall.why: The gap typically grows like the square root of the flips (about 800 for a million), but 800 out of a million is less than 0.1%, so the share is very close to 50%.
